questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Cross Product of Two Vectors Whose Angle Is a Special Angle
questions.problem: The vector $u$ has magnitude $5$, the vector $v$ has magnitude $3,$ the angle between $u$ and $v$ is ${90}^{∘}$ and $n$ is the unit vector that points in the direction of $u\times v.$ Find $u\times v$ in terms of $n.$
questions.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the cross product and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u\times v & =|u|\cdot |v|\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot n \\  & =5\cdot 3\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{90}^{∘}\cdot n \\  & =15\cdot 1\cdot n \\  & =15n.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Cross Product of Two Parallel Vectors
questions.problem: The vector $a$ has magnitude $3.$ What is $a\times a?$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose $a$ and $b$ are nonzero vectors. Then, $a\times b=0$ if and only if $a∥b.$

Notice that any vector is parallel to itself. So, we have $a∥a.$

Therefore, $a\times a=0.$

canonical_examples.problem: The vector $\mathbf{a}$ has magnitude $7,$ the vector $\mathbf{b}$  has magnitude $3,$ and the angle between the vectors is $120^\circ$ and $\mathbf{n}$ is the unit vector that points in the direction of $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}.$ Find $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}$ in terms of $\mathbf{n}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We use the formula for the cross product and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\times b & =|\,a\,|\cdot |\,b\,|\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cdot n \\  & =7\cdot 3\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘}\cdot n \\  & =7\cdot 3\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot n \\  & =\frac{21\sqrt{3}}{2}n.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Cross Product of Two Parallel Vectors
canonical_examples.problem: The vector $\mathbf{a}$ has magnitude $4,$ the vector $\mathbf{b}$ has magnitude $6,$ and $\mathbf{a} \parallel \mathbf{b}.$ Find $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Suppose $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ are nonzero vectors. Then, $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{0}$ if and only if $\mathbf{a} \parallel \mathbf{b}.$

Therefore, $\mathbf{a} \times \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{0}.$
